caption: The drawing features a brown jug or pitcher with a rounded body, a narrow neck, and a wide, circular mouth. The jug has a single large handle attached from the upper neck to the midsection of the body. Around the top part of the jug, just below the mouth, there is a circular band with a series of evenly spaced small holes, and three horizontal spouts or tubes protruding outward from the band. There is text embossed in capital letters on the jug’s body that reads: "HEAR. GENTLEMEN. COME. TRY. YOUR. SKILL. I’LL. HOLD. A. WAGER. IF. YOU. WILL - THAT. YOU. DON’T. DRINK. THIS. LIQUOR. ALL. WITHOUT. YOU. SPILL. OR. LET. SOME. FALL." The jug is illustrated in a gradient of light to darker brown shades, showing a glossy ceramic surface. In the upper left corner of the image, there is a smaller outlined technical drawing showing the jug’s front view, side view, and dimensions. The background is plain and light-colored, and beneath the jug, the same rhyme is written out again in red, capitalized type. A signature with the name "James H. Lawson" and a date is in the lower right of the drawing.
title: Trick Drinking Mug
